title: سبعون ألف ملك
sources: Jami' at-Tirmidhi 969 (authenticated by al-Albani, Sahih al-Jami' 5767) · Qur'an 90:17 (recited by Nasser Al-Qatami, everyayah.com)

beats.voice: زيارةٌ واحدة... يُصلّي عليكَ بها سبعونَ ألفَ مَلَك.

subs.text: …and seventy thousand angels pray for you.

beats.voice: مريضٌ تعرفُه... قريبٌ، أو صديقٌ، أو جار.

subs.text: Someone you know who is ill: a relative, a friend, a neighbour.

beats.voice: تجلسُ عندَهُ دقائق، وتدعو لهُ بالشفاء.

subs.text: You sit with him for a few minutes and pray for his recovery.

lines.html: «مَا مِنْ مُسْلِمٍ يَعُودُ مُسْلِمًا غُدْوَةً، إِلَّا صَلَّى عَلَيْهِ سَبْعُونَ أَلْفَ مَلَكٍ حَتَّى يُمْسِيَ…»

subs.text: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“No Muslim visits a sick Muslim in the morning except that seventy thousand angels pray for him until evening…”<small>Tirmidhi 969 · authenticated by al-Albani</small>

beats.voice: وإن زُرتَهُ مساءً... صلَّتْ عليكَ الملائكةُ حتّى تُصبِح. وفي القرآنِ الكريم:

subs.text: And if you visit him in the evening, the angels pray for you until morning.

lines.html: ﴿ثُمَّ كَانَ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَتَوَاصَوۡاْ بِٱلصَّبۡرِ وَتَوَاصَوۡاْ بِٱلۡمَرۡحَمَةِ﴾
سورة البلد · الآية ١٧ · بصوت ناصر القطامي

subs.text: “Then he is among those who believe, and urge one another to patience, and urge one another to compassion.”<small>Qur’an 90:17 · recited by Nasser Al-Qatami</small>

beats.voice: زُرْ مريضًا اليوم. وأرسِلْها لمن تُحبّ.

subs.text: Visit someone who is ill today. And send this to someone you love.
